Stage 2 · Explore a well · Simulated test world: dataset A

What the sensor said, what the model saw through it.

Eighteen wells from dataset A: the best, a typical and the hardest well of each hidden type, and three wells whose level sensor failed. For each, the raw readings, the model's weekly estimate of the true level, the simulated true level the model never saw, and its twelve-week forecast from any Sunday of the test year.

How to read it
  • Raw readings are start-of-session levels as logged: noisy, often taken before the well recovered, sometimes from a faulty sensor.
  • The model's estimate each week uses only data up to that Sunday.
  • The forecast is issued on the chosen Sunday and runs twelve weeks ahead with 20 possible rain years.
  • The true level is what the simulator knows; the model is scored against it.
Why these wells

Wells were picked by the model's twelve-week error on the test year, so the "hardest" ones show where it fails: mostly slow ridge and low-yield wells whose readings never show the full recovery. See What did not work.

Borewell Forecast is a proof of concept for forecasting groundwater levels in Bengaluru borewells. Results are labelled by where the data came from: vendor export (15 days, July 2026, in the vendor's real format but with demonstration water-level values), synthetic test system (450 simulated wells with a known answer) or digital twin (a physics-based simulation of the 579 wells over a year). No real water-level measurement has been used yet, and nothing here is yet a validated field forecast.
